messages:
maya: Heads-up — proposing we temporarily defer onboarding of the FalconLite-v3 candidate for next sprint. Benchmarks are noisy and there are customer risk asks. TL;DR: want alignment on criteria to pause vs ship small-scope onboarding.

devon: +1 to discussing. What specifically is noisy? latency or quality?

liza: Quality drift on long-form summarization tests. Variance across seeds is ~6-8% on our benchmark set (see sample below). Not sure it's an infra fluke.

maya: It looks like both. In latency traces we see occasional 2-3x tails on encoder warmups when KV cache hits are low. Quality on our summarization eval jumps between 72 and 80 depending on prompt seeds.

alex: Can we separate shipping the model to catalog (internal GA) vs enabling it for customer pinning? Maybe catalog entry with a note: "experimental, do not pin"?

maya: That’s one option. The ask from sales is they want to offer it to a pilot customer who requires pinning for compliance.

sam: Customer X is asking because FalconLite-v3 has specific tokenizer behavior they need. They said it's fine to be experimental but they need guaranteed version pin for the trial window.

devon: If we allow pinning now, we need a rollback/fallback path. Our smart routing can fallback to FalconLite-v2 but that will change outputs — potential for customer surprise.

liza: Also worried about our eval cadence — current automation didn’t catch the drift because the seed sampling was too small. I recommend re-run with N=40 seeds and updated prompts.

maya: Proposed options: 1) Defer pinning until we stabilize (re-run + infra fixes) — offer customer a canary on dedicated infra with explicit caveats. 2) Allow pinning with a mandatory pin-exception contract + SLOs and a short TTL (30 days). 3) Catalog-only release flagged as "preview" and no pining allowed. Thoughts?

alex: Option 2 is risky for ops, but might be acceptable if legal signs a pin waiver. Option 3 is lowest operational cost.

sam: From CS POV, customer prefers option 2 but will accept option 1 if we give them a timeline. They need a 2-week trial starting May 15.

devon: Operational constraints: to support option 2 we need a fallback plan plus automated rollback tooling. ETA to ship the rollback script and routing policy is ~6 business days.

liza: ETA for robust eval re-run with N=40 seeds is 3 business days if I get a GPU slot. If we see consistent regression, we should block pining.

maya: Ok — decision flow suggestion: if re-run (by 4787654330) shows <3% variance and no median regression, allow a catalog preview + pilot canary on dedicated infra (option 1-ish). If variance remains >3% or median drops, we hold and offer a timeline.

alex: Fine with that gate. We should also draft a short comms blurb for the catalog entry: include "preview" flag, known issues, and pin policy (no pin without exec signoff).

devon: I'll prioritize the rollback script. Ping me when liza's run is done and I'll start canary infra prep.

liza: Kicked off the N=40 seed runs now — will post results here.

opsbot: deploy-bot: benchmark-job-4787654321 started on infra/bench-queue (job id 2024-05-23-9876)

maya: Thanks team. Action items: liza -> finish re-run (3d), devon -> rollback script (6 business days), alex -> draft catalog blurb + pin-exception template, sam -> confirm customer trial flexibility. We'll reconvene after liza posts results.

sam: Noted. I'll give Customer X the tentative plan and ask if trial can shift to May 22 if needed.

liza: Results posted: median quality 74.5 (baseline v2: 76.1), variance across seeds still ~5.9%. Looks like model underperforms baseline on long-form by ~1.6 pts and variance is borderline.

maya: Given that, per our gate we should hold on pinning. Offer the canary preview on dedicated infra (no pin) and give customer the option to wait for a stability pass.

sam: Customer accepts preview-only for now, will wait on pin until stability is addressed. They want a status update in 7 days.

alex: I'll publish the preview catalog entry today with the issues and explicit "no pin" policy.

devon: Rolling backlog: will still start rollback tooling but deprioritize immediate canary automation.

maya: Thanks — closing this thread for the decision. We'll open a new ticket for the stabilization spike and track customer follow-up. :thumbsup:
